target_customer: VR and AR developers, then consumers, buying hand tracking and haptic gloves
problem: VR controllers do not capture fine finger movement or give fingertip feedback, which limits realism and precise interaction.
business_model: Hardware sales, developer kits priced at 250 USD in 2018
product_category: VR and AR haptic input gloves

founders.name: Charles Duffy
founders.background_notes: No biography found on the YC page or in press.

competitors.name: Manus VR
competitors.what: Finger tracking VR gloves with a developer kit
competitors.traction_then: Developer kit announced at 250 USD in March 2016

competitors.name: Noitom Hi5
competitors.what: VR gloves tracking fingers using the Vive tracker

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining finger tracking, fingertip actuators and compatibility with several tracking systems in a small glove is hard hardware work for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: No evidence of patents or exclusive technology, and several better funded glove makers were already shipping dev kits.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platform makers later improved controllers and hand tracking. Plexus itself faded from press after 2018.

market_need_then: VR developers wanted finger-level input and haptics; multiple glove startups drew press and funding in 2016 to 2018, but the installed base of VR headsets was small.

branding.domain_note: Company used plexus.im; that domain is now listed for sale at 4888 USD (checked 2026).
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, Road to VR and others at the 2018 unveiling; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name overlaps with a large engineering firm and a multi-level marketing company; a Road to VR comment noted the overlap. Brand had little visible reach beyond launch coverage.

outcome_analysis: Plexus unveiled a 250 dollar VR and AR glove dev kit in mid 2018 and raised only a small seed through YC. No coverage after 2018 was found, the website domain is now for sale, and no shutdown or acquisition report exists, so the outcome and cause are not public.
notes: YC directory says Active but the company website is only a domain sale page. Unverified: CB Insights lists a seed of about 120K (dated 2018-07, investors Y Combinator and StartOut Growth Lab) and PitchBook about 125K; both are aggregators, so no round is recorded. YC page says London; press says San Francisco. Founding year 2015 from a single aggregator. Completeness pass: Round added from CB Insights (seed 2018-07-25); rests on a single database. A 2018 Startups.co.uk awards profile says the founders were self-funded, which conflicts.
